model: LQM S W 3 R 120/277 EL N M6 (LQM stencil exit, white, red letters, nickel-cadmium emergency)
notes: Single-face LED exit sign for 120/277 V; this EL N version has the nickel-cadmium battery and the AC-only versions have none. Whole-sign input for the red emergency version: 0.71 W and max 0.05 A at 120 V, 0.92 W and max 0.06 A at 277 V.

gaps: The 1.2 V battery voltage is in the battery table of the 2017 family sheet only; neither sheet gives a cell count or capacity, so none is claimed.
The LED is described as using less than one watt; that is a ceiling, not a rating, so no w is set on the LED part.
The input watts and amps are for the whole sign, not a charger rating, so they are in notes and not on the charger.
The sheet does not say which diagnostic features come standard on EL N and which need the SD option, so the test switch and indicator are described as the sheet words them.
The two revisions (02/16/17 and 03/09/21) agree on the emergency input values and on the nickel-cadmium 90-minute battery line.
No circuit board parts are claimed, because the sheets name none.
No maker-hosted copy was readable: the img.acuitybrands.com PDFs and the Acuity product page returned 403.
method: Lithonia LQM LED exit sign spec sheet (Acuity Brands, Rev. 02/16/17, two pages), read from the copy on USESI (brochure 127149) with tools/research.js pdf; page 2 rendered and the battery and input tables checked.

Lithonia Contractor Select LQM spec sheet (Rev. 03/09/21, two pages), read from the HD Supply copy: its catalogue table has the exact number LQM S W 3 R 120/277 EL N M6 (red exit with backup battery, white), the input watts and amps, and the EL N ni-cad line.
Replacement battery pages were not opened.

comps.spec: Sealed, maintenance-free nickel-cadmium battery, 1.2 V in the battery table, 90-minute capacity to the emergency lamps
Exit LED lamp on printed circuit boards, low energy consumption of less than one watt, typical life 10 years; runs from AC in normal mode and from the battery in emergency mode

Constant-current series charger with two-state charge that recharges automatically after a discharge; current-limiting circuitry protects the circuit boards from shorts; the sheet also lists a line-latch (AC/LV reset) and a low-voltage disconnect
Test switch on the emergency (EL N) models; the family sheet describes it as manually starting a 30-second diagnostic test
Status indicator on the emergency (EL N) models; the family sheet describes a single multi-chromatic LED showing charging, test activation and diagnostic status
Engineering-grade thermoplastic housing, UL94V-0 flame rating, white on this catalogue number; unibody snaps together without fasteners, faceplate and back cover interchangeable
No lead-acid pack; the EL N battery is nickel-cadmium (ni-cad)
